questions.q: Why was the voyage on the Tankadere so dangerous?
choices: She was a tiny boat on stormy Chinese seas in November
Her crew had never sailed outside the Hong Kong harbour before
Pirates were known to attack small boats along that coast
The boat was old and had a leak that the crew could not fix
questions.evidence: This voyage of eight hundred miles was a perilous venture on a craft of twenty tons

questions.q: The sails above Aouda "seemed like great white wings," and the boat "seemed to be flying." What is the author comparing the boat to?
choices: A bird
A train
A kite
A cloud
questions.evidence: which rode on the waves like a seagull

questions.q: Why did the pilot hang out his lights at night?
choices: So that Aouda could read in the cabin below the deck
To avoid a collision in seas crowded with other vessels
To signal the Carnatic that they were coming behind her
Because the law of Hong Kong said every boat must do so

questions.q: What did Fix believe was Fogg's real reason for going around the world?
choices: To reach America safely by a long route and enjoy the stolen money there
To visit Aouda's family and arrange a marriage with her
To win the wager and then go straight back to his quiet life at the club in London
To find his lost servant somewhere in the ports of Asia
questions.evidence: he had traversed three quarters of the globe, so as to gain the American continent more surely

questions.q: What did Fix decide he would do if Fogg reached the United States?
choices: Give up and go home
Never lose sight of him until he was extradited
Hand the case to an American detective
Tell Aouda the whole truth and ask her to help him catch Fogg
questions.evidence: he would not lose sight of him for an hour

questions.q: What did Fogg and Aouda hope had happened to Passepartout?
choices: That he had gone back to the hotel and was waiting there
That he had boarded the Carnatic by mistake
That the police had found him and would send him to Shanghai
That he had taken a train across China to meet them
questions.evidence: the man might have embarked on the Carnatic at the last moment

questions.q: Why did Fix find it hard to eat Fogg's food?
choices: He was too sea-sick to keep anything down at all
He hated living at the expense of the man he wanted to arrest
He thought the food on the little boat might have been poisoned by Fogg
He had promised himself to eat only once a day
questions.evidence: To travel at this man's expense and live upon his provisions was not palatable to him.

questions.q: What did Fogg say when Fix offered to pay his share of the boat?
choices: "You may pay me back in Yokohama, sir."
"This enters into my general expenses."
"Pay the pilot whatever you think is fair."
"I will accept fifty pounds, and no more."
questions.evidence: This enters into my general expenses.

questions.q: Why did the crew of the Tankadere work so hard?
choices: They were afraid of what Fix might do to them
They hoped to win the reward Fogg had promised
They wanted to beat the Carnatic to Japan for fun
The pilot had threatened to fire them all
questions.evidence: inspired by the reward to be gained

questions.q: Which signs told John Bunsby that a storm was coming?
choices: A jumpy barometer and long surges from the south-east
Thousands of seabirds flew over the boat toward the shore
The water turned cold and a thick fog rolled in from land
Other fishing boats were hurrying back to the harbour
questions.evidence: The barometer announced a speedy change

questions.q: Why was Fogg glad to hear the typhoon came from the south?
choices: A south wind would be warm and pleasant for Aouda
It would carry the boat forward toward Shanghai
It meant the storm would be short and gentle
It would keep Fix in the cabin out of his way
questions.evidence: Glad it's a typhoon from the south, for it will carry us forward.

questions.q: How did the pilot prepare the boat for the typhoon?
choices: He took down most sail and raised one small storm-jib
He dropped anchor in a bay and waited for it to pass
He hoisted every sail he had to outrun the storm
He tied all of the passengers safely to the masts with strong ropes
questions.evidence: A single triangular sail, of strong canvas, was hoisted as a storm-jib

questions.q: Where did the passengers choose to stay during the storm?
choices: Below in the cabin
On the deck
In the pilot's hut
In the bow, tied up
questions.evidence: Neither Mr. Fogg, Fix, nor Aouda consented to leave the deck.

questions.q: When the pilot wanted to head for a port on the coast, which port did Fogg name?
choices: Hong Kong, the port they had left
Shanghai, where they were already going
Nagasaki, at the south of Japan
Macao, the Portuguese town nearby

questions.q: How did Aouda behave during the terrible night of the storm?
choices: She cried and begged the pilot to turn back
She was exhausted but did not complain
She hid in the cabin and would not come out
She helped the crew pull in the heavy ropes
questions.evidence: Aouda was exhausted, but did not utter a complaint.

questions.q: Why were the people on board so worried at noon on the last day?
choices: They had 45 miles to go in six hours and the wind was dying
The boat had sprung a leak and was slowly filling with water
They had run out of food and fresh water during the storm
Fix had been washed overboard by a giant wave
questions.evidence: the wind was becoming calmer every moment

questions.q: What did they see when they were still three miles from Shanghai?
choices: The Carnatic coming in from Yokohama
The steamer leaving for Yokohama
A police boat sent out to meet them
Passepartout waving from the river bank
questions.evidence: It was the American steamer, leaving for Yokohama at the appointed time.

questions.q: Why did Fogg have the flag hoisted at half-mast before firing the cannon?
choices: It was a signal of distress that might make the steamer come to help
It showed respect for the sailors lost in the typhoon that week
It told the harbour police in Shanghai that the boat was English
It was a way to greet the captain of the steamer as a friend
questions.evidence: this being the signal of distress

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: A small boat's race through a typhoon to try to reach the steamer in time
Fix finally telling Fogg that he is a detective sent from London
Aouda and Fogg exploring the coast of China on a pleasure trip
The crew of the Tankadere refusing to sail into the storm
questions.evidence: So the Tankadere kept steadily on her northward track.
